brief: Morgan Stanley now expects two more 25bp Fed hikes, in December 2026 and March 2027, for a terminal range of 4.25-4.5% in 1Q27, up from its prior view of 50bp total tightening entering the meeting. The dot plot showed a median of one more hike this year and a hold next year, but 8 of 18 participants see a third hike in 2027. Three signals drove the more hawkish call: Chair Warsh framed the September hike as removing a dose of accommodation, implying policy is not yet restrictive; he cited geopolitics, including Middle East conflict and rising oil and commodity prices, as a new driver of his reaction function; and the neutral rate estimate in the projections was revised up to 3.25% from 3.06%, meaning a given nominal rate represents less restraint than previously assumed. MS says an October hike cannot be ruled out given elevated market pricing, but also flags that a de-escalation in the Middle East or faster disinflation could leave only one more hike, in December. Rates, FX, MBS and muni desks each attach trade ideas to this hawkish read.
